title: Removal of a Fuel Boost Pump Inlet Filter Assembly

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of one boost pump inlet filter assembly from inside the wing tank, including the defuel, purge and entry control that must be complete before the access panel is opened.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove one boost pump inlet filter assembly from the wing tank, for element replacement or for inspection of the deposit on the mesh.
sections.job_setup_note: The tank must be defuelled, purged and certified safe for entry by the responsible person before the access panel is opened. Entry control must be in place with a standby person outside the panel at all times. Have the sample container ready before the element is disturbed, because the deposit on the mesh is the evidence and it will be lost if the element is handled dry. One person works inside the tank and one stays outside.
sections.procedure: 1. Defuel the affected tank and do the purge procedure. 2. Get the tank entry certificate from the responsible person. WARNING: DO NOT ENTER THE TANK UNTIL THE ENTRY CERTIFICATE IS ISSUED AND THE STANDBY PERSON IS IN POSITION. THE TANK ATMOSPHERE CAN BE FATAL. 3. Open the tank access panel in zone 591 or zone 691 as applicable. 4. Continue the forced ventilation for the full time given in the standard practice. 5. Disconnect the electrical connector at the pump 41QA and put a protective cap on it. 6. Release the clamp at the inlet duct 7953QT and move the duct clear. 7. Remove the self-locking nuts EN968165-23 from the filter housing flange. CAUTION: SUPPORT THE HOUSING BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE LAST NUT. THE HOUSING IS HEAVIER THAN IT LOOKS AND WILL DAMAGE THE PUMP INLET IF IT DROPS. 8. Take the housing D2820117143540 clear of the pump inlet. 9. Put the element in the sample container without cleaning it. 10. Do a general visual inspection of the pump inlet face and of the regulator D2820116810419 mounting. 11. Fit a blanking cap to the pump inlet.
sections.close_out: Send the element and the sample container to the laboratory if a deposit is present. Keep the tank ventilated and the entry control in place. Record the element condition and the pump inlet face condition on the aircraft work card. Do not close the access panel until the replacement housing is installed and the leak check is done.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Post MOD-163011 aircraft carry the longer 74 micron element in the taller housing; the flange pattern is the same.

safety_precautions: Do not enter the tank without a valid entry certificate.
Keep a standby person outside the access panel at all times.
Keep the forced ventilation running for the whole task.
